mcqs.question: Two parallel lines l₁ and l₂ are cut by a transversal t. The angles at the upper left intersection are numbered 1 (top left) and 2 (top right); the angles at the lower right intersection are numbered 3 (bottom left) and 4 (bottom right). Which pair of angles are alternate interior angles?
mcqs.explanation: Alternate interior angles lie between the two parallel lines and on opposite sides of the transversal. In the described figure, angles 1 and 3 satisfy this condition, making them alternate interior angles. The other pairs are either corresponding or exterior angles.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify interior angles on the same side of a transversal
mcqs.question: In the same configuration as above, which pair of angles are interior angles on the same side of the transversal?
mcqs.explanation: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal are the consecutive interior (or same‑side interior) angles. Angles 2 and 3 lie between the parallel lines and on the same side of the transversal, so they are the required pair. The other options are either not both interior or are on opposite sides.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines corresponding angles when a transversal cuts two parallel lines?

options.A: Angles that lie on opposite sides of the transversal and inside the parallel lines
options.B: Angles that occupy the same relative position at each intersection of the transversal with the parallel lines

mcqs.answer: Angles that occupy the same relative position at each intersection of the transversal with the parallel lines
mcqs.explanation: Corresponding angles are formed in matching corners at the two intersections; they have the same shape and measure when the lines are parallel. Option B captures this definition. Options A describes alternate interior angles, C is false (corresponding angles are equal, not supplementary), and D describes a different relationship.

mcqs.learning_point: Determine whether lines are parallel from angle relationships
mcqs.question: A transversal cuts two lines. One interior angle on the left side of the transversal measures 70°, and the interior angle on the same side of the transversal on the other line measures 110°. Are the two lines parallel?

options.A: Yes, because the interior angles on the same side sum to 180°
options.B: No, because the interior angles on the same side sum to 180°
options.C: Yes, because a pair of alternate interior angles are equal
options.D: No, because a pair of alternate interior angles are not equal

mcqs.answer: Yes, because the interior angles on the same side sum to 180°
mcqs.explanation: When a transversal creates interior angles on the same side that add up to 180°, the two lines are parallel (consecutive interior angle theorem). Here 70° + 110° = 180°, confirming parallelism. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: Line PQ cuts two distinct lines AB and CD at points P and Q respectively. Which line is the transversal?
mcqs.explanation: A transversal is a line that intersects two (or more) other lines. In the described situation, line PQ meets both AB and CD, so PQ is the transversal. AB and CD are the lines being intersected, not the transversal.

mcqs.question: In a diagram, a transversal t meets line l at point X forming angle 1, and meets line m at point Y forming angle 5. Angle 1 and angle 5 are equal. What type of angles are they?
mcqs.explanation: When a transversal cuts two lines, angles that occupy the same relative position at each intersection are corresponding angles. Equality of such a pair indicates the lines are parallel. They are not alternate interior (which lie on opposite sides of the transversal) nor vertical (which are formed by two intersecting lines at the same point).

mcqs.question: Statement: "If a pair of alternate interior angles formed by a transversal are equal, then the two lines intersected by the transversal are perpendicular." Is this statement true or false?

options.C: Cannot be determined without more information
options.D: Only true when each angle measures 90°

mcqs.explanation: Equal alternate interior angles imply that the two lines are parallel, not perpendicular. Perpendicular lines would create right angles, but the equality of alternate interior angles alone does not guarantee right angles. Therefore the statement is false.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify interior angles on the same side of a transversal
mcqs.question: If the sum of the interior angles on the same side of a transversal is 180°, what can be concluded about the two lines intersected by the transversal?

options.C: The two lines intersect at a right angle
options.D: No definite conclusion can be drawn

mcqs.explanation: When consecutive (same‑side) interior angles formed by a transversal add up to 180°, the lines are parallel (consecutive interior angle theorem). The other options describe different relationships that are not implied by this angle sum.
